tldr: This is a pattern across independent work, not one event: early November brought an NVIDIA post on fitting a 124B MoE onto one DGX Spark and a Show HN project, MoEShift, claiming faster MoE inference with half the RAM. A Nov 13 arXiv paper then took the same data-movement problem to TPUs with a fused kernel that also balances uneven expert loads.
whats_new: Hugging Face (Nov 18) describes expert streaming in Transformers that runs a 180B-parameter MoE in 32GB of RAM, the largest model-to-memory ratio in this thread.
why_it_matters: MoE serving is bound by moving expert weights, not FLOPs, so memory traffic and expert load balance decide which models fit your hardware and how fast they run.

beats.headline: Large MoEs squeezed onto a DGX Spark and a Mac
beats.summary: Two unrelated projects attack the same RAM ceiling on single machines.

beats.headline: Fuse-All kernel targets data movement and expert imbalance on TPUs
Transformers streams experts: 180B parameters in 32GB of RAM

open_questions: What tokens-per-second does Transformers expert streaming reach at 32GB, and on which storage tier?
Do the DGX Spark and MoEShift results publish RAM and throughput figures others can reproduce?
Does the Fuse-All kernel's load balancing ship in a public TPU serving stack?
take_for_builders: Before sizing hardware for an MoE, measure peak memory and expert-load traffic with streaming on and off; parameter count alone will mislead you.
